text:
sam-infra: Heads up — seeing a weird combo where HPA is firing and creating more replicas, but the cluster autoscaler isn't provisioning GPU nodes. Pods go Pending with nodeAffinity for nvidia-gpu, CA logs say 'no capacity in zone' then nothing. Any ideas?

autoscaler-bot: CA event: scaleUp forbidden: quotaExceeded for nodepool-gpu-us-west1. Details: insufficient regional quota (GPUs).

mei-sre: Oof, quota exhaustion + HPA can create a spike of Pending pods that CA can't satisfy. Can you paste the HPA and the external metric config? Also check the external-metrics adapter latency — we've seen Prometheus scraping lag cause bursts. :eyes:

sam-infra: HPA YAML snippet we use (trimmed):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-serving-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    kind: Deployment
    name: model-server
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 50
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: model_qps
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "100"
```
We're using model_qps as an external metric reported by our exporter (sum of QPS across shards).

kiran-platform: That 'sum across shards' smells like double-counting: HPA averageValue expects per-pod average when using AverageValue. If metric is a sum, it will drive HPA too aggressively. Also CA quota errors are the blocker — CA won't provision if region quota is 0. We had a runbook to fall back to preemptible pool when quota is low.

daniel-ml: Confirming — the exporter reports a cluster-wide QPS gauge. For 10 pods, gauge=1000 -> HPA thinks 1000/ (pods?) Wait, AverageValue semantics: when using External metric with AverageValue the controller divides by number of pods in targetRef. But since we're sending a non-pod-scoped metric (no labels), behavior is unpredictable across versions. TL;DR: we should send per-pod QPS (model_qps{pod}) or switch to AverageUtilization style.

mei-sre: Check adapter latency: run this PromQL to see staleness and scrape gaps:
```promql
rate(external_adapter_requests_total[5m])
up{job="external-metrics-adapter"}
```
If adapter returns stale values CA/HPA can see old low numbers then suddenly a big jump when it recovers -> big scale event. Also look at kube-controller-manager logs for hpa calculation.

sam-infra: Found something in the HPA controller logs: "external metric returned: 10000 (cluster-sum) -> desired replicas 100". We hit maxReplicas but many pods pending due to no GPU nodes. Then VPA suggested resource reductions which caused churn.

kiran-platform: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) change exporter to emit per-pod metric and use AverageValue properly, or 2) switch to External metric type with targetValue (cluster-level) and a custom scaler that translates to replica count. Also set HPA behavior to limit surge:
```yaml
behavior:
  scaleUp:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
    policies:
    - type: Percent
      value: 50
      periodSeconds: 60
```
This prevents instant huge replica jumps that CA can't satisfy.

daniel-ml: For quick fix, can we annotate deployment with: `autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-to-zero: \"false\"`? Not ideal. I'd rather throttle HPA and open a quota request with cloud for GPUs.

sam-infra: Raised quota ticket (cloud case 123456). In the meantime I've added a small reserved nodepool with 2 gpus in another region as fallback and updated CA config to prefer that pool on label fallback=gpu-reserve. Hoping CA will provision there if primary zone quota hits 0.

mei-sre: Good. Also add VPA exclusion annotation on the model-server for now: `vpa.k8s.io/exclude-objects: \"model-server\"` — VPA and HPA fighting can oscillate.

autoscaler-bot: Note: cluster-autoscaler event: scaleUp: using nodegroup 'gpu-reserve' to satisfy pending pods (if quota available).

sam-infra: After changes: exporter now emits `model_qps_per_pod{pod=...}` and HPA updated to target AverageValue 100. Added stabilizationWindow and limited percent policy. Observing smoother growth; CA provisioned reserve pool for 2 nodes. Will monitor for 2 hours. Thanks all :heart:

kiran-platform: Nice. Follow-ups: add a scripted test that simulates adapter lag + metric burst so HPA/CA behavior is validated in CI. Also add alert when Pending pods for >60s have GPU affinity.

daniel-ml: I'll update the exporter this afternoon and add unit tests to ensure we report per-pod metrics.

mei-sre: I'll add the alert and a Grafana panel for external adapter latency. If anything flares, ping #oncall. :pushpin:
